summary: Both sides are the same pattern — the whole 60-px strip held at one flat colour, breathing smoothly from black to full and back on a sinusoidal envelope — but the port's colour is pure cyan where the original's is a bluer azure, and its cycle is ~10% too fast (29.5 s vs 32.8 s).
observations: Structure identical and trivially simple on both sides: every --dump frame (t=0/3/6/9 s and t=23/24/24.3/25/29 s) has distinct=1 across all 60 pixels on BOTH sides — no gradient, no spatial feature, the strip is one uniform colour at all times. R is exactly 0 on both sides in every frame and every stats series.

Envelope shape is a match. Resampling one full cycle to 21 phase points and normalising to each side's own peak: orig 0.000 0.019 0.089 0.197 0.338 0.493 0.649 0.790 0.903 0.974 1.000 0.981 0.910 ... vs port 0.000 0.023 0.091 0.201 0.341 0.497 0.649 0.790 0.903 0.971 0.994 0.973 0.900 ... — both sit on (1-cos)/2 to within a couple of quantisation counts, and neither is a triangle. Symmetric rise and fall, a brief full-black dwell at the trough and a brief plateau at the peak on both.

COLOUR DIFFERS. Original's colour is fixed at G/B = 0.700 at every brightness (dumps: (0,90,128), (0,138,197), (0,171,244), (0,177,253)) — an azure / sky-blue, peaking at (0,178,255). Port's colour is fixed at G = B exactly (dumps: (0,128,128), (0,204,204), (0,249,249), (0,115,115)) — pure cyan, peaking at (0,255,255). The hue gap is ~18 deg of output hue (orig ~198 deg, port 180 deg) and is obvious with the two waterfalls side by side.

PERIOD DIFFERS. Measured from rising half-max crossings over a 300 s / 2 fps window, 9-10 cycles per side, the period is rock steady on both: orig 32.786, 32.714, 32.786, 32.786, 32.786, 32.714, 32.786, 32.786 s (mean ~32.78 s); port 29.500, 29.500, 29.497, 29.500, 29.448, 29.500, 29.500, 29.500, 29.458 s (mean ~29.49 s). Port is 11.1% faster; over 300 s it completes 10 fades where the original completes 9.
The two start nearly in phase (at t=0 both are ~52% of peak and rising) and drift apart by roughly a third of a cycle per 100 s, so a fixed --skip window can land them in opposite halves of the fade.

Peak mean brightness 144 (orig) vs 170 (port) is entirely explained by the hue difference — both saturate their brightest channel at 255 at the peak — so the brightness ENVELOPE amplitude matches; only the chroma differs.
No frame-rate coupling on either side: at 5, 10 and 40 fps the first rising half-max lands at 32.60/32.70/32.73 s (orig) and 29.30/29.40/29.45 s (port). Both are time-based, not frame-stepped.
Fully deterministic and seed-independent: seed 1 vs seed 7 over 60 s gives a max meanBrightness difference of 0 on both sides, so nothing here is RNG-driven.
Steady state is healthy on both: over 300 s neither amplitude nor period drifts, no decay, no saturation, no runtime or compile errors on either side.
Control surfaces match: the engine reports zero settable controls for BOTH sides, and --probe-controls found nothing to probe. No missing/extra/renamed dial.
feedback: Fix the hue. The original holds a constant azure/sky-blue with G/B = 0.700 at every brightness level, peaking at RGB (0,178,255); the port holds pure cyan with G = B, peaking at (0,255,255). The port needs its hue nudged ~18 deg toward blue so that at full brightness green comes out around 178, not 255 — the red channel is already correctly 0 on both.

Slow the fade by ~11%. The original's full black-to-full-to-black cycle takes 32.78 s (very close to 32.768 s, i.e. an exact power-of-two-flavoured interval); the port's takes 29.49 s. Both are perfectly steady, so this is a fixed rate constant, not drift or jitter.

Nothing else needs changing: the spatial behaviour (one flat colour over the whole strip), the sinusoidal fade shape, the full-black trough, the fps-independence, and the absence of controls all already match the original exactly.
